initial_decision.rationale: All four candidates are direct/near-direct matches to alcohol dependence: PGS002738 and PGS002739 explicitly target “Alcohol use disorder” with trait_efo “alcohol dependence”, while PGS000201/PGS000202 are “Problematic alcohol use” but their phenotyping_reported is still alcohol use disorder (DSM-5 criteria count). Among these, PGS002738 has the most directly aligned trait_efo (“alcohol dependence”) and provides the strongest visible discrimination-style evidence via an OR (top 10% vs rest) of 1.96 (CI 1.54–2.51) in a European evaluation sample (n=7,900). However, the overall evidence remains limited/incompletely comparable across candidates: none report PRS-only AUC/R², covariates are unknown for PGS002738/PGS002739 (reducing comparability), and PGS000201/PGS000202 report only small ΔR² values on a DSM-5 criteria-count phenotype rather than a clear case-control AUD endpoint. These limitations prevent a high-confidence ‘best’ direct-match selection.

final_decision.rationale: CONFIRM pick of PGS002738. The heritability lookup for alcohol dependence shows low-to-moderate SNP h2 in EUR (best local match h2_obs≈0.036; other nearby records up to ~0.098), which mainly serves as a sanity ceiling for PRS-only R2/AUC. None of the four candidates report PRS-only R2/AUC that could be checked against this ceiling, so h2 does not reveal a contradiction or covariate-driven inflation that would undermine the picker’s choice. Given the available evidence, PGS002738 remains the most defensible direct-endpoint option: it matches alcohol dependence/AUD at the trait_efo level and provides the strongest visible PRS-linked discrimination-style signal (OR top 10% vs rest = 1.96 in EUR evaluation, n=7,900). The remaining limitations noted by the picker still apply (unknown covariates for PGS002738/PGS002739; PGS000201/PGS000202 only small ΔR² on a DSM-5 criteria-count phenotype), keeping confidence at Moderate rather than High.

initial_decision.rationale: All 6 candidates are direct matches (trait_reported/trait_efo and phenotyping_reported all indicate abdominal aortic aneurysm). However, the pool has limited PRS-comparable performance reporting: most models report only full-model AUROC/C-index (often with unknown or non-comparable covariates), and only two provide PRS-comparable metrics (PGS001784 reports Nagelkerke R2 with covariates regressed out; PGS002054 reports partial-r). PGS000753 is preferred because it provides a clear PRS effect-size estimate (OR per SD 1.37, 95% CI 1.30–1.44) with basic covariates (age, sex, PCs), supporting standalone PRS signal without heavy clinical packaging; competing models either lack PRS-isolated metrics/effect sizes (PGS003429/PGS003972) or report high full-model discrimination that is not directly comparable to PRS-only performance (e.g., PGS003973 C-index 0.882 with age/sex). Confidence is moderate (not high) because PGS001784 does provide an explicit PRS-comparable R2 in a very large European evaluation sample, making it a meaningful competitor, and the available metrics across candidates are not directly harmonized.

final_decision.rationale: Heritability sanity-check does not reveal a flaw in the picker’s choice. The best-matched EUR LDSC estimate for abdominal aortic aneurysm is very low on the observed scale (h2_obs ~0.0003; liability h2 ~0.02), so very high full-model discrimination metrics in the pool (e.g., C-index 0.882 for PGS003973; AUROC 0.868 for PGS001784) are plausibly dominated by age/sex and other covariates rather than PRS signal, and should not be treated as PRS-comparable evidence. Among candidates, PGS000753 provides a clean, standalone PRS signal via an OR per SD of 1.37 (95% CI 1.30–1.44) with only basic covariates (age/sex/PCs), avoiding obvious clinical-risk packaging. The main competitor, PGS001784, does report a PRS-comparable Nagelkerke R2 (covariates regressed out) of ~0.0147, which remains below the liability-scale h2 ceiling and is therefore not heritability-incoherent; however, this does not create an h2-anchored contradiction that would force revising away from PGS000753, given the overall comparability limitations and covariate-heavy full-model AUROC reporting across the rest of the pool.
